cohort: The study included 2181 women who had an HSG, with 494 (22.6%) having an abnormal HSG, and subsequently achieved clinical pregnancies (232 in the abnormal HSG group and 814 in controls).
finding: An abnormal HSG, particularly uterine abnormalities, was associated with an increased risk of preeclampsia and low birthweight, while tubal abnormalities were linked to a heightened risk of preterm labor.
